title: US Army First Aid Manual FM 4-25.11

provenance.notes: Official public domain United States Government medical field publication

sections.title: Stopping Severe Bleeding
sections.text:
Severe arterial bleeding is an immediate life threat that must be controlled immediately:
1. Direct Pressure: Place a sterile field dressing or clean cloth directly over the wound and apply firm, steady manual pressure with both hands for at least 5 to 10 minutes.
2. Pressure Dressing: Maintain pressure by securing the dressing tightly with an elastic wrap or roller bandage. Check pulse below the dressing to ensure circulation is not entirely cut off unless a tourniquet is intended.
3. Tourniquet: Apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound (never over a joint) for severe limb amputations or when direct pressure fails to stop catastrophic arterial bleeding. Tighten until bleeding stops and record the time of application on the patient's forehead (e.g. 'T 14:30').

sections.title: Treating Shock
sections.text:
Shock is a depression of vital body functions resulting from severe blood loss, burns, or severe trauma.
Symptoms: Pale or clammy skin, rapid weak pulse, confusion, rapid shallow breathing, extreme thirst.
Treatment:
1. Position the casualty flat on their back and elevate feet 6 to 12 inches unless head or chest injuries exist.
2. Loosen restrictive clothing at neck, waist, and boots.
3. Prevent chilling or overheating by covering with a blanket or poncho.
4. Reassure the casualty and keep them calm. Do not give fluids if unconscious.
